about: Sub-shetachim: a regional director's area under a head shliach. They show only with the map's Sub-shetachim switch, never on the head shluchim's map (owner, Oct 26: "I meant as a separate thing to toggle to see sub shetachim not in the head shluchim part"). Each is drawn with borders of its own, round its member houses (owner, Nov 1: "why are you using county situations you should be drawing your own borders"): members are listed (members: chabad.org ids), or are the parent shetach's houses within membersIn (US counties by Census GEOID, L.A. Times neighbourhoods by region or name, county subdivisions by name in one county, { box: [west, south, east, north], county? } (a box, or the part of a county in it), or { near: [lon, lat], km }), less exclude; mushrooms never count. areas: whole areas of the map added as they are (the Baja peninsula). reach / join (km, optional): how far round each house it reaches (3), and the gaps it bridges (up to twice 6). Most shetachim have none, and none fills its shetach: the rest stays the head shliach's own. scripts/build-sub.mjs makes web/data/sub.json (npm run build runs it).

subShetachim.name: San Diego & Baja
subShetachim.head: Yonah Fradkin
subShetachim.source: Chabadpedia (יונה פרדקין): the Rebbe's shliach in San Diego since 5736, "המשמש גם כשליח אזורי ומנהל תחתיו מערך מסועף של שלוחי הרבי", 26 couples under him in San Diego County as of 5782. The Baja peninsula is his too (owner, Oct 26: "baja peninsula is under fradkin"). Drawn round the county's houses (the metro, North County and the east county's towns), not the whole county's desert; and the peninsula's two states whole.

subShetachim.name: The Valley
subShetachim.head: Mordechai Einbinder
subShetachim.source: Chabad of the Valley (Tarzana). Its staff page (2004) lists its houses across the San Fernando Valley (Encino, Tarzana, Porter Ranch, North Hollywood, Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Woodland Hills, Calabasas, Chatsworth, Northridge, CSUN) and, under it, the Conejo (Rabbi Moshe Bryski, "Conejo Regional Director": Agoura, Westlake, Oak Park, Thousand Oaks), Ventura (Rabbi Yakov Latowicz), Simi Valley (Rabbi Noson Gurary) and the Santa Clarita Valley (Rabbi Choni Marozov), each called "Regional Director". Its founder, Rabbi Joshua B. Gordon, passed away 29 Shevat 5776 (Chabadpedia). The Jewish Journal (May 2, 2024) calls Rabbi Mordechai Einbinder the "leader of the sprawling Chabad of the Valley community based in Tarzana", 32 institutions. Its members, the houses on that list (the owner, Nov 1: "What about that 2004 thing? I'm sure that's still accurate as well"): those in the San Fernando Valley (the L.A. Times' region), Calabasas and Hidden Hills; the Conejo (Agoura Hills, Westlake Village, and Ventura County's Thousand Oaks county subdivision: Thousand Oaks, Newbury Park, Oak Park, North Ranch); Simi Valley; the Santa Clarita Valley; and Ventura (a part of its own, past Camarillo and Oxnard). Not Oxnard or Camarillo (the owner: "Oxnard and Camarillo are way way past the valley"; each has its own house, not on the list), nor Moorpark or Ojai. Drawn round those houses, not the county lines (the owner: "why does it stretch so North").

subShetachim.name: Southern Nevada
subShetachim.head: Shea Harlig
subShetachim.source: Chabad of Southern Nevada, founded in 1990 by Rabbi Shea and Dina Harlig, with its affiliated houses around Las Vegas (Summerlin, Green Valley, the East, Southwest, the Hebrew Center and UNLV: the Chabad Times, April 2000, in UNLV's special collections; a 2014 UNLV oral history: as its director he "has helped establish seven Chabad locations throughout the community"). Drawn round its houses in the Las Vegas valley, not all of Clark County.

subShetachim.name: Northern Nevada
subShetachim.head: Mendel Cunin
subShetachim.source: The owner, Nov 1: "Do northern Nevada under Cunin". Chabad of Northern Nevada in Reno, Rabbi Mendel Cunin its director (chabad.org), and the houses round it: Chabad Cares and the Learning Center (Reno), Chabad at UNR, Chabad of Carson City (Rabbi Levi Sputz) and Chabad at Lake Tahoe (Rabbi Mordechai Richler, Stateline). Its members: the houses in Washoe County, Carson City and Douglas County.

subShetachim.name: Tucson
subShetachim.head: Yossie Shemtov
subShetachim.source: The owner, Nov 1: "Tucson/Vail is Shemtov no?". Chabad Lubavitch of Tucson, Rabbi Yossie Shemtov its executive director (chabad.org), and the houses round it: Chabad on River (Rabbi Ram Bigelman), Chabad of Oro Valley (Rabbi Ephraim Zimmerman), Chabad of Vail (Rabbi Yisroel Shemtov), the University of Arizona's Chabad House (Rabbi Shmulie Shanowitz) and Chabad of Cochise County (Rabbi Benzion Shemtov, Sierra Vista: a part of its own). Its members: the houses in Pima and Cochise Counties.

subShetachim.name: Saint Petersburg
subShetachim.head: Mendel Pewzner
subShetachim.source: The owner, Nov 1: "Peterburg under Pewsner". Rabbi Mendel Pewzner, the Jewish Community of St. Petersburg at the Grand Choral Synagogue (chabad.org). Its members: Berel Lazar's shetach's houses within 45 km of the city's centre.

subShetachim.name: Long Island
subShetachim.head: Tuvia Teldon
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Tuvia and Chaya Teldon, regional directors of Chabad Lubavitch of Long Island since 1977 (Anash; COLlive, "In for the long haul"); Lubavitch.com (Sept 2025): "over 29 Chabad rabbis in 23 Chabad centers throughout Long Island". Its headquarters: Lubavitch of Long Island, Commack. Its members: the houses in Nassau and Suffolk Counties.

subShetachim.name: Northwest New Jersey
subShetachim.head: Asher Herson
subShetachim.source: The Jewish Link: "Rabbi Asher Herson, regional director of the Chabad Center of Northwest NJ" (Rockaway); chabad.org lists its branches as "Chabad of Northwest NJ – Western Region" (Flanders, Rabbi Yaacov Shusterman) and "Chabad of Northwest NJ – Berkshire Valley" (Wharton, Rabbi Levi Naparstek). Its members: those three, and the houses in Sussex and Warren Counties (Chabad of Sussex County).

subShetachim.name: St. Louis
subShetachim.head: Yosef Landa
subShetachim.source: chabad.org: "Chabad of Greater St. Louis Regional Headquarters", Rabbi Yosef Landa its "Co-Founder and Regional Director"; the St. Louis Jewish Light calls him and his wife Shiffy its regional directors. Its members: the houses in St. Louis County, the City of St. Louis and St. Charles County (Chabad of St. Charles County: his son Rabbi Chaim Landa).

subShetachim.name: Northern Virginia
subShetachim.head: Sholom Deitsch
subShetachim.source: JNS: Rabbi Sholom Deitsch, "regional director of Chabad Lubavitch of Northern Virginia"; the Washington Jewish Week: he and his wife Chanie opened it in January 1991 and "expanded to eight more Chabad locations throughout Northern Virginia from 2001 to 2021, including Alexandria, Loudoun County and Springfield". Its members: the houses in Fairfax, Arlington, Loudoun and Prince William Counties and the cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, Falls Church, Manassas and Manassas Park.

subShetachim.name: South Broward
subShetachim.head: Raphael Tennenhaus
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Raphael Tennenhaus, "director of Chabad activities in south Broward"; Chabad of South Broward is headquartered in Hallandale, a network of "11 Chabad centers in South Broward" (TorahCafe; the Jewish Press). Its members: Broward County's houses south of Fort Lauderdale (Hallandale Beach, Hollywood, Dania Beach, Davie, Cooper City, Pembroke Pines). Asked of the owner: whether Chabad Lubavitch of Southwest Broward (Rabbi Pinny Andrusier, Cooper City) and his sons' houses are his or a network of their own.

subShetachim.name: Greater Orlando
subShetachim.head: Sholom Dubov
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Sholom Ber Dubov, "Head Shliach to the Greater Orlando Area"; Chabad of Greater Orlando, founded 1984 (Maitland), its own pages: "Senior Rabbi & Executive Director". Under him: Rabbi Tzviky Dubov for Maitland, Winter Park, Casselberry, Oviedo and Winter Springs, his son-in-law Rabbi Yanky Majesky's Chabad of North Orlando (Lake Mary, Sanford, Longwood), and the seventh location, Altamonte Springs (2019); three of his wife's siblings "were appointed by Rabbi Dubov and work as emissaries in Central Florida" (Heritage Florida Jewish News; chabadorlando.org). Its members: the houses in Orange, Seminole and Osceola Counties.

subShetachim.name: Greater Austin
subShetachim.head: Yosef Levertov
subShetachim.source: Chabad of Greater Austin, directed by Rabbi Yosef and Rochel Levertov, and its branches: "The six Chabad centers in Austin include Chabad of Austin, the Rohr Chabad Jewish Student Center at the University of Texas at Austin, Chabad of South Austin, Chabad Young Jewish Professionals (YJP) and Downtown Austin, Chabad of Round Rock and Chabad of Leander", led by his son-in-law and sons (Shalom Austin; Anash). Its members: the houses in Travis, Williamson and Hays Counties.

subShetachim.name: Greater Mercer County
subShetachim.head: Dovid Dubov
subShetachim.source: The Rabbinical College of America (New Jersey's regional headquarters) appointed Rabbi Dovid Dubov "to oversee Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Mercer County", its executive director; with the Friendship Circle of Greater Mercer County (Rabbi Shmuel Dovid Wilhelm) and the county's other houses (RCA; New Jersey Jewish News). Its members: the houses in Mercer County.

subShetachim.name: Bucks County
subShetachim.head: Yehuda Shemtov
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Yehuda Shemtov, executive director of Lubavitch of Bucks County (Newtown; Wikipedia on Rabbi Abraham Shemtov), with its branch Lubavitch of Central Bucks County West (Doylestown, Rabbi Mendel Prus; chabad.org) and the county's other houses. Its members: the houses in Bucks County.

subShetachim.name: Staten Island
subShetachim.head: Moshe Katzman
subShetachim.source: Chabad Lubavitch of Staten Island, Rabbi Moshe and Chana Katzman (chabad.org; its school, Mrs. Chana Katzman principal), and the island's houses run by their family: Chabad of the South Shore (Rabbi Levi Katzman), Chabad of Tottenville (Rabbi Mendel Katzman, serving Charleston, Pleasant Plains and Prince's Bay), associate director Rabbi Mendy Katzman (ChabadInfo; CrownHeights.info). Its members: the houses in Richmond County.

subShetachim.name: Sarasota & Manatee
subShetachim.head: Chaim Steinmetz
subShetachim.source: Chabad Lubavitch of Sarasota and Manatee Counties, Rabbi Chaim Steinmetz (IRS; the Sarasota Mikvah), "three centers, a Mikvah, a preschool and a school" (CrownHeights.info), and his family's houses: Chabad of Downtown Sarasota (Rabbi Levi Steinmetz; Lubavitch.com, Dec 2025) and Bradenton (Rabbi Zev Steinmetz; chabad.org). Its members: the houses in Sarasota and Manatee Counties.

subShetachim.name: Tampa
subShetachim.head: Yossie Dubrowski
subShetachim.source: Chabad Lubavitch of Tampa Bay, Inc. (1988), Rabbi Yossie and Sulha Dubrowski, with its school; its South Tampa branch, Chabad Chai (Rabbi Mendy and Nechama Dina Dubrowski) (IRS; chabadchaicenter.com). Pinellas County has its own Chabad of Pinellas County, so it isn't in it. Its members: the houses in Hillsborough County.

subShetachim.name: North Broward & South Palm Beach
subShetachim.head: Yosef Biston
subShetachim.source: Chabad-Lubavitch of North Broward and South Palm Beach: Rabbi Yosef Biston its "executive vice president" (chabad.org), its headquarters chabad.org's "Chabad of Parkland – Regional HQ for North Broward & South Palm Beach"; he founded the Chabad Center of Margate in 1985 under that heading (a 2000 Chabad postcard). Its members: Broward County's houses north of Fort Lauderdale (Coral Springs, Parkland, Margate, Coconut Creek, Tamarac, Pompano Beach, Deerfield Beach, Lighthouse Point) and Palm Beach County's south of Boynton Beach (Boca Raton, Delray Beach), as the office's name has it.

subShetachim.name: Inland Empire
subShetachim.head: Sholom Harlig
subShetachim.source: Chabad of the Inland Empire (Rancho Cucamonga), "since its inception in 1989 under the direction of Rabbi Sholom and Chanie Harlig" (its own site), with the Chabad Jewish Center of Chino Hills (Rabbi Mendy Harlig, 2020). Its members: the houses in San Bernardino County. Riverside and Temecula aren't in it: no source ties them to it.

subShetachim.name: Montgomery County
subShetachim.head: Shaya Deitsch
subShetachim.source: Lubavitch of Montgomery County (Fort Washington), Rabbi Shaya Deitsch its executive director, who "also supervises groups in Rydal and Chestnut Hill" (the Philadelphia Inquirer, 2013); its own site lists the Fort Washington headquarters, Rydal (Rabbi Zushe and Dini Gurevitz) and Lafayette Hill, with a Friendship Circle (jewishmc.com). Its members: Montgomery County's houses north of the Main Line (Fort Washington, Rydal, Lafayette Hill), within the county: not the Main Line's (a network of their own) nor Philadelphia's.

subShetachim.name: Atlantic County & the Shore
subShetachim.head: Shmuel Rapoport
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Shmuel Rapoport "oversees Chabad of Atlantic County, which runs Chabad at the Shore in Margate" (Ventnor; chabad.org: its executive director); his family's houses round it: the Ventnor shul (Rabbi Avrohom Rapoport), Chabad of Stockton University (Galloway, Rabbi Meir Rapoport), and Cape May County's programmes in Wildwood (COLlive; the Jewish Link). Its members: the houses in Atlantic and Cape May Counties.

subShetachim.name: Passaic County
subShetachim.head: Michel Gurkov
subShetachim.source: The Chabad Center of Passaic County (Wayne), Rabbi Michel Gurkov, and its branches run by his family: the Chabad Center for Jewish Life of Upper Passaic County (Wanaque, Rabbi Mendy Gurkov, serving North Passaic County), Chabad Passaic Clifton, and its preschool; Rabbi Mayer Gurkov joined it for its preschool and the county's outreach (the Jewish Standard; chabad.org). Its members: the houses in Passaic County.

subShetachim.name: Dallas
subShetachim.head: Mendel Dubrawsky
subShetachim.source: Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky, "regional director of Chabad-Lubavitch of Dallas" (in Dallas since 1984); new houses "joining the larger growing network of Chabad Houses under the auspices of Chabad of North Texas and the leadership of Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky" (the Park Cities); "11 [Chabad Houses] in Dallas" (a Texas Chabad source); his son Rabbi Levi Dubrawsky's campus centre (UNT/DFW), Preston Hollow and the Friendship Circle (chabadofdallas.com; DOJLife; CrownHeights.info). Its members: the houses in Dallas, Collin, Denton and Rockwall Counties. Not Fort Worth and Tarrant County (Chabad of Fort Worth & Tarrant County, a name of its own).

subShetachim.name: Howard County
subShetachim.head: Hillel Baron
subShetachim.source: The Lubavitch Center of Howard County (Columbia), Rabbi Hillel Baron, and the county's houses round it, his family's: Chabad of Ellicott City (Rabbi Yanky Baron), Clarksville and Laurel (Chabad Ellicott City's own list of its four centres); "the 5 Chabad centers in Howard County" (a Howard County government document). Its members: the houses in Howard County.

subShetachim.name: South Dade
subShetachim.head: Yakov Fellig
subShetachim.source: Chabad of Miami (Coconut Grove; "Serving Miami's Jewish Community since 1989"), Rabbi Yakov Fellig its director (chabad.org), and its branches page, "13 Branches Across South Dade": Downtown Coral Gables, Kendall & Pinecrest, Cutler Bay & Homestead, Chabad at UM (Coral Gables and South Miami), UM Jackson, West Kendall and the rest (chabadmiami.com). Its members: Miami-Dade's houses south of downtown and west of the bay (Coconut Grove, Coral Gables, South Miami, Kendall, Pinecrest, Palmetto Bay, Cutler Bay, Homestead, Key Biscayne): fourteen listings, its thirteen branches and their schools. Not Miami Beach or North Miami.

subShetachim.name: Southwest Florida
subShetachim.head: Yitzchok Minkowitz
subShetachim.source: Chabad Lubavitch of Southwest Florida (Fort Myers), "under the leadership of Rabbi Yitzchok Minkowicz", its director, "officially welcomed new emissaries" (the Jewish Federation of Greater Naples' Federation Star, June 2025); its houses round Fort Myers: Cape Coral, Bonita Springs & Estero, FGCU, the Israeli Center (chabad.org). Its members: the houses in Lee County. Not Naples (Chabad of Naples, Rabbi Fishel Zaklos, since 2004) nor Charlotte County (its own director): no source ties them to it.

subShetachim.name: South Area
subShetachim.head: Menachem Gurkow
subShetachim.source: Shaloh House Chabad of the South Area (Stoughton, 1991), Rabbi Menachem Mendel Gurkow its co-executive director, "committed to reach out to as many Jewish families and individuals as possible in the south of Boston area", serving Canton, Easton, Sharon and Stoughton; new shluchim were appointed to serve the South Area, Brockton and Randolph among them (GuideStar; CrownHeights.info). Its members: the houses of Stoughton, Canton, Sharon, Easton, Randolph and Brockton.

subShetachim.name: North Fulton
subShetachim.head: Hirshy Minkowicz
subShetachim.source: Chabad of North Fulton (Alpharetta), Rabbi Hirshy Minkowicz: it serves Alpharetta, Crabapple, Duluth, Johns Creek, Milton and Roswell, with "satellite offices in Roswell, Johns Creek, and Alpharetta" (the Atlanta Jewish Times' synagogue guides; chabadnf.org). Its members: north Fulton County's houses (Alpharetta, Roswell). Not Gwinnett's or Forsyth's, each its own.

subShetachim.name: Western Monmouth
subShetachim.head: Boruch Chazanow
subShetachim.source: Chabad Lubavitch of Western Monmouth County (Manalapan), Rabbi Boruch and Tova Chazanow, its executive director: "the Holmdel Chabad is a branch of this organization" (the Jewish Link, 2025); it runs Yeshiva Bais Menachem and a Chabad Jewish Center at Brookdale Community College (CrownHeights.info; NJJN). Its members: Monmouth County's houses west of the shore (Manalapan, Freehold, Marlboro, Holmdel, Morganville).

subShetachim.name: East Valley
subShetachim.head: Mendy Deitsch
subShetachim.source: Chabad of the East Valley (Chandler, 1997), Rabbi Mendy and Shterna Deitsch, and the centre it opened in Ahwatukee: "We realized more Jews were attending our programs and we saw a need for a center over there" (Jewish News of Arizona; CrownHeights.info). Its members: those two. Mesa, Gilbert, San Tan Valley and ASU aren't in it: no source makes them its branches.
